correctness.rationale: The simultaneous zero gcd case is excluded: the only equal positive-index consecutive Fibonacci values are both 1. The quadratic Fibonacci invariant evaluated at the common shifted residue −a forces G_a(n) to divide a²+(−1)^n and hence a⁴−1. Subtracting the two original arguments replaces one divisibility condition by d|F_(n−1). Strong divisibility gives n−1=j z(d), including j=0. The Fibonacci matrix at z(d) is u_d I mod d, with u_d²=(−1)^z(d), so the remaining condition is u_d^j=−a; eligibility and the unique class follow. Equivalently L_d is the Pisano period modulo d, since the matrix first returns to I at z(d) times the scalar unit order. A nonempty single class forces every period on n≥1 to be a multiple of L_d: take any positive representative and add the proposed period. Recovering the gcd from all its divisor predicates proves the converse and the lcm, while Möbius inversion gives the full exact value law. Independently enumerating the complete modular orbits at a=3,9,−9 (lengths 120,240,240) and checking cyclic periods gives 60,60,120 and the stated a=3 histogram. The uploaded verifier was inspected but not run; the proof supplies all shifts.
residual_risks: No complexity guarantee for factoring a⁴−1 or computing ranks; no claims for unequal shifts or different gaps.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the all-shift exact least period through eligible divisor events, and the ensuing value frequencies. Rahn–Kreh explicitly pose the same general least-period question after treating ±3. The closest inspected broader theorems provide sufficient Pisano-type periods, in some examples strictly larger than the true periods. Known rank and scalar identities are inputs, and generic lcm and Möbius steps are not new in themselves. The additional step is using orbit membership for each divisor and recovering sharp global minimality from all occupied local classes; no inspected theorem gives this solution for every eligible a.
residual_risks: Spilker's chapter could not be inspected in full; later restatements do not rule out additional content.
An equivalent unindexed orbit or prime-power formulation of the general solution remains possible. Chen's ±2 cases are relevant prior art in addition to the frozen record's cited special cases.

value.rationale: This gives an explicit all-parameter answer to a prior published least-period question, replacing a potentially nonminimal sufficient period with a sharp, locally computable invariant, and supplies an exact frequency law instead of sample histograms. The criterion isolates why sign can change the least period even while the ambient Fibonacci modulus remains unchanged. The motivation is the exact period and value spectrum of the naturally bounded equal-shift family, not invention of the standard algebraic tools used in the proof.
residual_risks: The formula is effective, not an efficiency guarantee for large shifts.
